$comment: Validates _source/property-items.json, which is the single source of truth for table T-016.

NO DISPLAY NAME LIVES HERE. FR-038 (MUST NOT) keeps every word the screen prints in one dictionary per language, so a property item's shown name is display-words.json's `properties` section, keyed by the same PR row id.
NO CANDIDATE, BOUND OR DATE-NESS LIVES HERE EITHER. The note under table T-016 (MUST NOT) forbids copying what grs-document.schema.json and DATE_COLUMNS already hold.
title: The property item manuscript
description: The rows of table T-016, in print order. FR-006 (MUST) makes that order the order the panel draws, so the array's order IS the specification.

$comment.description: Notes for whoever edits this manuscript. JSON carries no comments, so the role declaration goes here -- one line per note, the same shape settings.json uses. Check 21 reads the first of them. Not rendered.

items.description: One entry per row of table T-016, in the order the panel prints them.

id.description: The row id of table T-016. The only join a display name, a test or the panel may use.

columns.description: The GRS JSON column names this row edits, in the order they are drawn. One row may carry several (PR-3 carries start and finish).

inputKinds.description: The 入力の型 of each column, one per entry of `columns` and in the same order. FR-006 (MUST) makes this what the control is drawn as.

isReadOnly.description: Whether the panel refuses to edit this row. Absent means editable, which is what FR-006's STATEMENT makes the default.

appliesTo.description: Which selection this row belongs to. FR-006 (MUST) makes the panel print only the rows whose appliesTo matches what is selected, and forbids printing the others -- without it a TaskGroup's height would be drawn on a Task's panel, because the array's order IS the print order and every row in it would be printed. Absent means Task, which is what every row of table T-016 was until 2026-09-02.

prose.description: A cell of the printed document, per language. The manuscript belongs to no language, so the ja/en split is data entry rather than a second copy.
